object.title: Discover what supported Arc exports actually contain
object.build: Inspect owner-authorized Arc exports and document versions, supported fields and limits before promising a converter.
accept: Retain export provenance and inert fixtures; distinguish portable exports from Dia's direct installed-browser import.
Enumerate observed Spaces/Favorites/Profile/split/session fields without inventing absent structures.
Record unsupported data and a proposed mapping/preview contract for owner review; keep originals unchanged.
object.disposition: Recommended core integration or verification, with improvements preferred over literal Arc replication.
object.referencePlatforms: Reference platform support is limited to the cited source. Documentary macOS or Windows coverage does not prove native behavior; Linux is a downstream design and verification target.
object.referenceNote: The linked reference documents/release histories describe this workflow family. Acceptance below specifies the intended improved Arcified behavior.
object.openQuestions: Native integration, failure behavior and applicable platform results must be proven for this slice; unavailable checks stay open.
object.readiness: Proposed work after native/reference prerequisites and explicit decisions in this issue.

retrievalLimitations: Original assignment inbound-import article 19335089616791 returned HTTP 404 from both page and public article API. Its title concerns import into Arc and does not establish an Arc export.

Migration and sunset HTML page fetches were inaccessible in web tooling; migration page HEAD returned HTTP 403 with Cloudflare challenge. The documented public Help Center article API returned successful JSON responses without authentication.
Search results from third-party sites were used only as discovery leads. Their format or feature claims were not accepted as primary evidence.
No browser, reference app, owner account, installed browser data, large installer, native build, benchmark or remote CI was used.
Documentation revision timestamps identify article revisions, not exporting Arc app builds or a versioned export grammar.
